summary: Console TTFT for streaming chat is lower than client-measured TTFT (inconsistent reporting)
description:
Customer report (Northbridge Support): Console shows significantly lower TTFT than what their client observes for streaming chat requests. They are using SDK streaming (SSE) and measuring TTFT as time from HTTP request start to receipt of first streamed chunk.

Issue summary
- Console metric: TTFT (streaming) appears ~150–350ms faster than customer client measurements for same time window.
- This is causing confusion during their internal SLO review (they track p95 TTFT) and undermines trust in Console perf reporting.

Impact
- Customer perceives Redwood Console latency reporting as inaccurate.
- Risk: escalations / contract SLA questions if we can’t explain discrepancies.

Environment
- Dedicated cluster: northbridge-prod
- Region: us-east
- Models impacted: Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct (primary), Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct (secondary)
- Streaming mode: SSE

Customer steps to reproduce (as provided)
1) Send streaming chat completion request with max_output_tokens=256.
2) Measure TTFT at client as: t_first_event_received - t_request_start.
3) Compare to Console chart “TTFT (p50/p95)” filtered to model + route.

Observed
- Client p95 TTFT: ~620ms
- Console p95 TTFT: ~340–450ms (varies by hour)

Expected
- Console TTFT should match server-side equivalent of “first streamed bytes sent” and be explainable relative to client measurement (network + buffering deltas), with documented definition.

Notes / references
- Related internal discussion on TTFT definition for streaming (server vs client clock) and first-token chunking behavior is happening in runtime/telemetry threads; we should align on one canonical definition for Console and baseline suite.

Support asks
1) Confirm Console’s TTFT definition for streaming.
2) Determine if telemetry is incorrect vs expected network/SDK buffering.
3) Provide customer-facing explanation and (if needed) fix + backfill guidance.
comments: 2026-02-06 (Nadia Rahman, Support): Opened after customer call. Northbridge attached client logs showing first SSE event consistently arrives ~200ms after server reports first token time in traces (they included request_id samples). Request IDs available if Eng needs them (shared via support secure note).

2026-02-06 (Logan Wright, Telemetry): Acknowledged. Initial guess: Console uses server-side TTFT based on first token generated timestamp, not first chunk sent. For streaming those can diverge if we buffer/coalesce tokens before emitting the first chunk. Pulling data from telemetry pipeline for the customer route to see if we have chunk-sent timestamps.

2026-02-07 (Julian Moore, Serving Runtime): Confirmed runtime currently records `ttft_ms` off “first token produced” in the streaming path. There is a separate internal event for “first chunk flush” but not consistently emitted for all streaming code paths (depends on chunking policy). If the SDK waits for a newline / JSON boundary, client-perceived TTFT can be later. However, customer says they count receipt of first SSE event, so server-side should ideally track `first_chunk_sent` for streaming.

2026-02-07 (Nadia Rahman, Support): Asked customer for clarification: they count TTFT on first SSE event regardless of content. They are not waiting for a newline; they parse events as-delivered. They also see the gap even on short prompts (<=50 tokens).

2026-02-08 (Logan Wright, Telemetry): Found inconsistency: Console chart uses metric field `ttft_ms` from runtime spans for both streaming + non-streaming, labeled simply as TTFT. In streaming, that field is populated before the first chunk is written to socket. We also observed one edge case where the timestamp used is post-buffer-flush in some instances, which explains why Console varies (different serving nodes / code path). Recommendation: instrument a dedicated streaming TTFT = time to first chunk sent, and update Console to use it for streaming routes.

2026-02-09 (Omar El-Sayed, Serving Runtime): Reproduced on staging with packet capture. Gap comes from: token produced -> buffered -> first SSE frame assembled -> write() -> kernel socket buffer -> client receives. Our metric currently stops at token produced. For customer trust, agree we should measure at “first chunk flush initiated” at least. Network will still add delta but should be smaller and stable. Also noted an edge case: first chunk timestamp can be overwritten when the first chunk is empty metadata frame; metric ends up using second frame.

2026-02-10 (Logan Wright, Telemetry): Looping in Nadia: we can offer customer a clear definition today (Console is server-side first-token-generated, not client-perceived first-event-received). But given inconsistency across nodes + edge case overwrite, this is also a bug. Creating a short-term fix PR in runtime to capture correct first streamed chunk timestamp and ensure we do not overwrite it. Then we can update Console mapping and run validation.

2026-02-11 (Julian Moore, Serving Runtime): Fix in progress. Added `stream_ttft_ms` computed off `first_chunk_sent_at` (monotonic clock), and fixed edge case for empty first frame (do not treat as first token event; still counts as first chunk sent if actually sent). PR opened: sources/github/redwood/pr-23944.json. Will backport to current runtime patch train if approved.

2026-02-12 (Nadia Rahman, Support): Drafted customer response: explained current TTFT definition and that we are shipping a fix so streaming TTFT aligns to time-to-first-streamed-chunk. Asked for 3 request IDs after fix deploy to confirm their numbers converge. Customer ok with plan, wants ETA.

2026-02-13 (Logan Wright, Telemetry): PR merged + runtime patch scheduled for Dedicated northbridge-prod during next maintenance window. Also adding a small telemetry validation harness as part of the perf baseline effort to continuously compare server timestamps to client probe measurements (ties to ongoing baseline initiative).

2026-02-14 (Nadia Rahman, Support): Confirmed with customer after deploy: Console p95 TTFT increased and now within ~40–90ms of their client measurement (expected network/SDK delta). Customer satisfied. Closing ticket.
resolution:
Resolved by correcting streaming TTFT instrumentation and aligning Console to a dedicated streaming TTFT metric.

Changes
- Serving runtime fix: record streaming TTFT as time-to-first-streamed-chunk-sent (and prevent overwrite/edge-case errors on first frame). Implemented in sources/github/redwood/pr-23944.json.
- Telemetry/Console: stop using generic `ttft_ms` for streaming routes; use `stream_ttft_ms` where available (initial rollout for Dedicated clusters).

Customer-facing outcome
- After deploy, Console TTFT is consistent with client-measured TTFT within expected network/SDK overhead.

Follow-ups
- Add ongoing validation harness (server vs client TTFT probes) to catch regressions in instrumentation.
- Document TTFT definitions (streaming vs non-streaming) in internal perf methodology docs and ensure baseline suite uses the same definitions.
